ideas.title: A boomerang that comes back
ideas.goal: as Lumi the player throws a carved boomerang (hold to wind up, the mouse sets tilt and aim) and it curves round the meadow and comes back, if they threw it right. Fun because it is a skill toy: the tilt, the spin and the wind decide the loop, a good throw is caught on the way back, a bad one lands in the pond or knocks a pear off a tree.
ideas.idea: No path is scripted. The boomerang is one rigid body with two wings; every step each wing is cut into blade elements, and each element gets lift and drag from its own air speed (forward speed plus spin times radius, so the advancing wing lifts more). That uneven lift makes a torque, the spinning body precesses, and precession is what turns the flight into a loop. Wind from wind.jl adds to the air speed. Elements run in one KernelAbstractions kernel on Mantle; the body steps in PrintSim as an affine body (which also proves its bodies can turn, the thing my climb trials could not show). Someone watching sees a wooden boomerang spin, lean, curve away over the friends and come back to Lumi's wing, with its path drawn faintly in the grass for the last throw.
ideas.form: physics/boomerang.jl + a jump-in key (O: throw) + a generated boomerang asset; traced film low over the meadow: throw, the loop, the catch

ideas.title: A rope you throw
ideas.goal: the player throws a coil of rope with a stone tied to its end; it wraps around whatever branch or post it hits, and then they swing on it across the pond, or tie a drifting boat to the dock. Fun because the rope goes where the world lets it: two wraps round a post hold a whole boat, one wrap slips, a bad throw tangles in a bush.
ideas.idea: The rope is a real rod: a chain of short segments with stretch and bend stiffness, stepped on the GPU (PrintSim's vertex block descent or an XPBD chain on Mantle), colliding with the island's real meshes through Raycore. Where it lies on a branch it slides or sticks by friction, and around a post the friction adds up turn by turn (the capstan law comes out of the contacts, it is not written in). Someone sees the rope fly, whip round a pine branch, Lumi swing out over the water on it, and the rope creak taut.
ideas.form: physics/rope.jl + jump-in key + film: one throw, the wrap, the swing over the pond

ideas.title: Drawing with the sun
ideas.goal: on a sunny day the player carries a glass lens and burns pictures into the dock planks and the fence: hold the bright spot still and the wood smokes and chars, move fast and it only warms. Fun because it is drawing with something real: clouds stop the pen, the spot is sharp only at the right height, and what you burn stays.
ideas.idea: The lens is real glass in the scene. Its focal spot comes from refracting sun rays through it (Raycore rays against the lens mesh); the spot's irradiance heats a heat grid on the wood's surface (a heat equation kernel on Mantle, wood's real conductivity and heat of charring), and wood that passes its char temperature darkens its texture for good, with smoke rising where it is burning. Path traced, the lens throws a real caustic. Someone sees a tiny white star on the planks, a curl of smoke, and a black line growing into Lumi's name.
ideas.form: plugin with a lens tool in jump-in + a heat kernel + a texture that keeps the burns; still of the burned dock, film of a word being burned

ideas.title: A smoke ring cannon
ideas.goal: the player thumps a barrel with a cloth drum and a smoke ring flies out across the meadow; aimed well it knocks a friend's hat off or blows out a lantern 10 m away. Fun because the rings are slow and visible, so you aim and lead your target, and two rings can crash into each other.
ideas.idea: The ring is a real vortex ring: a vortex filament (a loop of points carrying circulation) that moves itself by Biot-Savart induction, slows by air's viscosity, and carries smoke particles along its flow. Its push on a hat or a flame is the induced air speed there. Points and smoke run as kernels on Mantle; the smoke traces as a soft medium. Someone sees a white ring wobble across the grass, swell, hit a sheep's hat and spin it off.
ideas.form: physics/vortex.jl + a barrel prop + jump-in key; film of three rings, one hitting

ideas.title: Sky lanterns that really fly
ideas.goal: at night the player lights paper lanterns and lets them go; whether one rises depends on how hot its air gets and how heavy its paper is, and the wind carries them out over the sea. Fun because the friends make their own, some are too heavy and crawl along the grass, and a sky full of them is the island's best night.
ideas.idea: Each lantern is a paper bag over a small flame: the air inside heats by the flame and cools through the paper (Newton cooling), its density follows the ideal gas law, buoyancy minus weight minus drag moves it, and wind.jl pushes it. The paper bag is a PrintSim sheet that sags until the hot air fills it. In the tracer every lantern is a real warm light that lights the water under it.
ideas.form: plugin (night key, friends launch too) + traced film of the launch over the sea

ideas.title: Keep the campfire alive
ideas.goal: the player builds a campfire from sticks they gather, lights it and keeps it going through the night: too few sticks and it dies to embers, too many and it chokes, wind fans it. Fun because the friends come and sit around it, and a well-fed fire lights the whole beach.
ideas.idea: The fire burns real fuel: each stick has mass, heats up from its neighbours, pyrolyses past its temperature and gives heat and flame in proportion; air flow from the gaps between sticks feeds it. Sticks are PrintSim bodies that settle as they burn thin and the pile collapses. Flames are an emissive volume in the tracer; the light flickers with the burn rate.
ideas.form: plugin with gathering and a fire pit; film of the fire built, lit, collapsing to embers

ideas.title: Climb anything: the first real fall
ideas.goal: as Lumi the player jumps at any wall, trunk or rock, catches whatever edge the claws reach, shimmies along it and pulls up, to reach places nobody can (the cottage roof, the top of the big pine). Fun because the climb is read from the real shape of the world, and a bad grab is a real fall.
ideas.idea: This session's step: today I found that in my grab trials my body never turned, so a hold may just be a body that cannot tip. First make the simplest test tip over in PrintSim (a tilted box on the ground), then rerun the hinged grab with the pad landing on top of the round beam: a slow arrival should hold, a fast one slide off the curve and fall. Someone sees two side-on shots of Lumi, same beam, one hanging, one falling.
ideas.form: physics/climbgrab.jl + a traced film of hold and fall with Lumi's model on the PrintSim pose

ideas.title: Dominoes across the meadow
ideas.goal: the player stands planks, flower pots and pumpkins up in a line across the meadow and tips the first; the chain runs past the friends, round the cottage and ends ringing the bell. Fun because it is building something that you get to destroy, and a gap or a wobble breaks it.
ideas.idea: Every piece is a PrintSim rigid body with its real size and mass on the real ground, so spacing and height decide whether the next one falls; a heavy pumpkin can knock over a row, a light pot stops it. The player places pieces in jump-in with a key; friends cheer or get knocked over.
ideas.form: plugin (place key, tip key) + film of a long chain

ideas.title: Gold leaf
ideas.goal: the player lays gold leaf on a stone or a letter in the gallery: the leaf is thinner than paper, it floats, wrinkles and sticks where it touches, and rubbing it smooth makes it shine. Fun because the result is a real gilded thing that glints in the lantern light, and every leaf crumples differently.
ideas.idea: The leaf is a PrintSim sheet a tenth of a micron thick in look (the real one is far too thin to simulate, so a sheet with gold's density per area); air drag makes it hover, contact with the glue sticks it, wrinkles stay as folds. In the tracer it is a real gold conductor whose wrinkles break up the highlight; burnishing flattens the folds and the highlight gets sharp.
ideas.form: plugin at the gallery easel + traced still of a gilded letter by lantern light

ideas.title: Tug of war in the mud
ideas.goal: the player and a friend pull a rope against two others across a muddy patch; tap in rhythm to pull, lean back too far and your feet slide. Fun because it is funny to lose, the friends fall in the mud, and the rhythm matters more than mashing.
ideas.idea: The rope carries tension through a segment chain; each creature's feet hold by friction (mu times its weight, wet mud lower), its lean shifts how much weight is on its feet; whoever's feet slip first slides. Mud splashes as particles and leaves brown marks on the creatures that stay until rain.
ideas.form: mini game plugin + film of one round
